advances: For the original rank-one entropy rows with arbitrary positive integer height means and slack mean one, normalization by the height mean gives absolute covariance, tail, and directional fourth-moment bounds. These bounds give one absolute mean-halfspace cap for arbitrary independent products, with the constant applied once after summing all block variances.
author: research-agent
proof:
The deficit map and its inverse \(x=L-a-hy\) give the stated support bijection. The prescribed original means give \(\mathbb EA=L-j-hk=1\), \(\mathbb EY=k\); conversely, these deficit means give the original means \((j,k)\). Therefore proving an exact positive entropy law in deficit coordinates proves the corresponding assertion for the original law, without changing probabilities or entropy.

Write \(\mathcal T=\{(a,y)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{2}:a+hy\le L\}\) and \(Q=\lfloor L/h\rfloor\). The triangle with vertices \((0,0),(L,0),(0,Q)\) lies in \(\operatorname{conv}\mathcal T\). The assumptions give \(L\ge2\) and \(Q\ge101k+100>2k\), so \(1/L+k/Q<1\). Since both coordinates of \((1,k)\) are positive, it is in the interior of this triangle and hence in the interior of \(\operatorname{conv}\mathcal T\).

For \(t=(t_1,t_2)\), define \(F(t)=\log\sum_{(a,y)\in\mathcal T}e^{t_1a+t_2y}-t_1-kt_2\). Some Euclidean ball of radius \(\delta>0\) about \((1,k)\) is contained in \(\operatorname{conv}\mathcal T\). The maximum of \(t\cdot(z-(1,k))\) over \(z\in\mathcal T\) is consequently at least \(\delta\lVert t\rVert\), and \(F(t)\ge\delta\lVert t\rVert\). This proves coercivity. Its Hessian is the covariance matrix under the positive weights proportional to \(e^{t_1a+t_2y}\). The support contains \((0,0),(1,0),(0,1)\), so every nonzero linear functional has positive variance. Thus the Hessian is positive definite everywhere. The coercive strictly convex function \(F\) has a unique minimizer. At that minimizer the gradient vanishes, giving the exact full means \((1,k)\). Put \(r=e^{t_1}\), \(s=e^{t_2}\). This proves existence and uniqueness of the positive law and its two full-law parameter equations.

If \(p(a,y)=r^as^y/Z\) is this law and \(q\) is any other law on \(\mathcal T\) with means \((1,k)\), the equality of means gives
\[
\sum_{q(a,y)>0}q(a,y)\log\frac{q(a,y)}{p(a,y)}=H(p)-H(q)\ge0.
\]
Indeed, \(-\log z\ge1-z\), applied with \(z=p(a,y)/q(a,y)\), bounds the sum below by \(1-\sum_{q(a,y)>0}p(a,y)\ge0\). Equality requires \(p=q\) on the support of \(q\) and that support to have all the mass of the strictly positive law \(p\), hence requires \(q=p\). This proves uniqueness of the entropy maximizer. Substitution of \(a=L-x-hy\) gives the asserted original exponential coordinates.

For an integer \(N\ge0\) and a positive parameter \(z\), let \(g_N(z)\) be the mean of the law on \(\{0,\ldots,N\}\) with weights proportional to \(z^a\). It is nondecreasing in \(z\), since its derivative is the variance divided by \(z\). It is increasing in \(N\), since a new endpoint is strictly above the previous mean. For \(0<z<1\), the finite geometric series gives
\[
g_N(z)=\frac{z}{1-z}-\frac{(N+1)z^{N+1}}{1-z^{N+1}},\qquad
g_7(2/3)=\frac{10562}{6305}>\frac32.
\]
All the conditional distributions used next are conditionals of the original law. They are not assigned the original full means.

Markov's inequality and \(\mathbb EY=k\) give \(\mathbb P(Y\le3k)\ge2/3\). On such a row, the conditional law of \(A\) has geometric weights \(r^a\) and cutoff \(L-hY\ge j-2hk+1\ge(98k+100)h+1\ge7\). If \(r\ge2/3\), its conditional mean on every such row would exceed \(3/2\). Nonnegativity on the other rows would imply \(\mathbb EA\ge(2/3)g_7(2/3)>1\), a contradiction. Hence \(r<2/3\).

Set \(q_k=2k/(2k+1)\). Markov's inequality and \(\mathbb EA=1\) give \(\mathbb P(A\le2)\ge2/3\). Given \(A=a\le2\), the conditional law of \(Y\) has geometric weights \(s^y\) and cutoff
\[
\left\lfloor\frac{L-a}{h}\right\rfloor\ge\left\lfloor\frac{j+hk-1}{h}\right\rfloor\ge101k+99\ge12k.
\]
Bernoulli's inequality gives \((1+1/(2k))^{2k}\ge2\). Consequently \(q_k^{12k+1}\le1/64\), and the finite geometric mean formula yields
\[
g_{12k}(q_k)=2k-\frac{(12k+1)q_k^{12k+1}}{1-q_k^{12k+1}}
\ge2k-\frac{12k+1}{63}\ge\frac{113k}{63}>\frac{3k}{2}.
\]
If \(s\ge q_k\), these conditional means and nonnegativity elsewhere would give \(\mathbb EY\ge(2/3)g_{12k}(q_k)>k\), a contradiction. Thus \(s<q_k<1\). Since both parameters are now below one, every finite geometric conditional mean is strictly smaller than the corresponding untruncated mean. Averaging over all rows gives \(1=\mathbb EA<r/(1-r)\), and averaging over all columns gives \(k=\mathbb EY<s/(1-s)\). Therefore \(r>1/2\) and \(s>k/(k+1)\). Finally, \(r^h\le r^2<4/9<1/2\le k/(k+1)<s\), so \(\eta=\log(s/r^h)>0\); also \(\lambda=-\log r>0\).

A geometric law of parameter \(z<1\), truncated to \(\{0,\ldots,N\}\), is stochastically dominated by the untruncated geometric law of parameter \(z\): for every integer \(0\le a\le N\), its cumulative probability is \((1-z^{a+1})/(1-z^{N+1})\ge1-z^{a+1}\). Untruncated geometric laws are increasing in their parameter by their tail probabilities \(z^a\). Apply these facts to every original conditional law of \(A\) given \(Y\), and then average the conditional tail inequalities. This proves that the entire original marginal \(A\) is dominated by a geometric variable of parameter \(2/3\). Apply the same facts to every original conditional law of \(Y\) given \(A\), and average, to dominate the entire marginal \(Y\) by a geometric variable of parameter \(q_k\). These are full-law marginal statements. The untruncated geometric tail formula gives the two stated tail bounds. Their exponential versions follow from \(1-z\le e^{-z}\), because \(2/3\le e^{-1/3}\) and \(k/(2k+1)\ge1/3\).

If a geometric variable has untruncated mean \(w\), its probability generating function is \(1/(1+w-wz)\), and differentiation at \(z=1\) gives falling-factorial moments \(\mathbb E(G)_a=a!w^a\). The polynomial identities \(G^2=(G)_2+G\) and \(G^4=(G)_4+6(G)_3+7(G)_2+G\) therefore give \(\mathbb EG^2=2w^2+w\) and \(\mathbb EG^4=24w^4+36w^3+14w^2+w\). The two dominating geometric variables have means respectively \(2\) and \(2k\). Thus
\[
\mathbb EA^2\le10,\qquad \mathbb EA^4\le730,\qquad
\mathbb E(Y/k)^2\le8+2/k\le10,\qquad
\mathbb E(Y/k)^4\le384+288/k+56/k^2+2/k^3\le730.
\]
Both \(A\) and \(Y/k\) have exact full mean one. Their centered second moments are consequently at most \(9\). For every nonnegative real \(z\), \((z-1)^4\le z^4+1\), so their centered fourth moments are at most \(731\). Cauchy-Schwarz pointwise, followed by \((z_1^2+z_2^2)^2\le2(z_1^4+z_2^4)\), proves
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb ED^2&\le(u^2+v^2)\mathbb E[(A-1)^2+(Y/k-1)^2]\le18(u^2+v^2),\\
\mathbb ED^4&\le2(u^2+v^2)^2\mathbb E[(A-1)^4+(Y/k-1)^4]\le2924(u^2+v^2)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]

It remains to establish the full covariance lower bound; conditional covariance assertions would not suffice. The partition function obeys \(Z\le1/((1-r)(1-s))<3(2k+1)\le9k\). The elementary expansion
\[
(1+1/k)^k=\sum_{a=0}^{k}\binom{k}{a}k^{-a}\le\sum_{a=0}^{k}\frac1{a!}<3
\]
uses \(a!\ge2^{a-1}\) for \(a\ge2\) to bound the remaining finite sum by a number strictly below one. It follows that \(s^k>(k/(k+1))^k>1/3\). Every point in the rectangle \(\{0,1\}\times\{0,\ldots,k\}\) belongs to the original deficit support because \(1+hk\le L\). Its original probability \(r^as^y/Z\) is greater than \(1/(54k)\): on the rectangle \(r^a>1/2\), \(s^y\ge s^k>1/3\), and \(Z<9k\).

Retaining exactly these original atoms in the nonnegative sum defining \(\mathbb ED^2\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb ED^2
&\ge\frac1{54k}\sum_{y=0}^{k}\left[\left(-u+v(y/k-1)\right)^2+\left(v(y/k-1)\right)^2\right]\\
&=\frac{k+1}{54k}\left[u^2+uv+\frac{2k+1}{3k}v^2\right]
\ge\frac{u^2+v^2}{216}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For the last inequality, \((2k+1)/(3k)\ge2/3\), \((k+1)/k\ge1\), and
\[
u^2+uv+\frac23v^2-\frac14(u^2+v^2)
=\frac34(u+2v/3)^2+\frac1{12}v^2\ge0.
\]
Because \(\mathbb ED=0\), this is the covariance lower bound about the exact original normalized mean. Combining it with the fourth-moment estimate gives \(\mathbb ED^4\le2924\cdot216^2(\mathbb ED^2)^2\), where \(2924\cdot216^2=136422144=K\). The centered original-coordinate identity follows from \(X=L-A-hY\). Its coefficient map \((b,c)\mapsto(-b,k(c-hb))\) is invertible because \(k>0\), so it supplies the claimed estimate for every original direction.

For the independent product, write its centered original directional summands as \(T_i\), and their variances as \(V_i\). Every \(T_i\) has mean zero and \(\mathbb ET_i^4\le KV_i^2\). Independence and centering give
\[
\mathbb ET^2=\sum_iV_i,\qquad
\mathbb ET^4=\sum_i\mathbb ET_i^4+6\sum_{i<j}V_iV_j
\le K\left(\sum_iV_i\right)^2,
\]
since \(K\ge3\). The constant is therefore applied once to the sum of all original block variances, with no factor depending on the number of blocks.

Suppose \(\sigma^2=\mathbb ET^2>0\). Holder's inequality applied to \(|T|^{2/3}|T|^{4/3}\) gives \(\sigma^2\le(\mathbb E|T|)^{2/3}(\mathbb ET^4)^{1/3}\), hence \(\mathbb E|T|\ge\sigma/\sqrt K\). For \(T_+=\max(T,0)\), \(T_-=\max(-T,0)\), the exact full centering gives \(\mathbb ET_+=\mathbb ET_-=(1/2)\mathbb E|T|\). Cauchy-Schwarz gives \(\mathbb ET_+\le\sigma\sqrt{\mathbb P(T>0)}\) and \(\mathbb ET_-\le\sigma\sqrt{\mathbb P(T<0)}\). Each strict one-sided probability is consequently at least \(1/(4K)\). If \(\mathbb ET^2=0\), the nonnegative variable \(T^2\) has mean zero, so \(T=0\) almost surely.

For each original row, \((j_i,k_i)\) has nonnegative integer coordinates and \(j_i+h_ik_i=L_i-1\le L_i\); the product mean is thus in the original product support. Write any closed halfspace containing this mean as \(H=\{z:w\cdot(z-\boldsymbol\mu)\ge a\}\), where \(a\le0\). Its centered projection is precisely a sum \(T\) with arbitrary original block coefficients. If the variance is positive, \(\{T>0\}\subseteq H\), giving the asserted cap. If it is zero, the original product lies in \(H\) almost surely. All these events and expectations refer to the product of the original laws with their exact original means.
statement:
Let \(h,j,k\) be integers with \(h\ge2\), \(k\ge1\), and \(j\ge100h(k+1)\), and put \(L=j+hk+1\). On the original set \(E_{(L,h,1)}=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{2}:x+hy\le L\}\), there is a unique strictly positive exponential law with the exact original full mean \(\mathbb E(X,Y)=(j,k)\). This is the unique Shannon-entropy maximizing law among all laws on that set having that mean.

For the original deficit \(A=L-X-hY\), the map \((X,Y)\mapsto(A,Y)\) is a bijection onto \(\{(a,y)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{2}:a+hy\le L\}\), and \(\mathbb EA=1\), \(\mathbb EY=k\). The original law has exactly the density
\[
\mathbb P(X=x,Y=y)=\frac{r^{L-x-hy}s^y}{Z(r,s)},\qquad
Z(r,s)=\sum_{y=0}^{\lfloor L/h\rfloor}s^y\sum_{a=0}^{L-hy}r^a,
\]
with no composition multiplicity. The unique positive parameters are specified by the full-law equations \(r\partial_r\log Z=1\), \(s\partial_s\log Z=k\), and obey
\[
\frac12<r<\frac23,\qquad
\frac{k}{k+1}<s<\frac{2k}{2k+1}<1.
\]
In original exponential coordinates the density is proportional to \(e^{\lambda x+\eta y}\), where \(\lambda=-\log r>0\) and \(\eta=\log s-h\log r>0\).

For every real \(t\ge0\), the full original marginals satisfy
\[
\mathbb P(A\ge t)\le(2/3)^{\lceil t\rceil}\le e^{-t/3},\qquad
\mathbb P(Y/k\ge t)\le\left(\frac{2k}{2k+1}\right)^{\lceil kt\rceil}\le e^{-t/3}.
\]
For all \(u,v\in\mathbb R\), define \(D=u(A-1)+v(Y/k-1)\). With expectations under this entire original law,
\[
\frac{u^2+v^2}{216}\le\mathbb ED^2\le18(u^2+v^2),\qquad
\mathbb ED^4\le2924(u^2+v^2)^2\le K(\mathbb ED^2)^2,
\quad K=136422144.
\]
Thus the covariance of the normalized original vector \((A,Y/k)\) lies between \(I_2/216\) and \(18I_2\) in positive-semidefinite order. Every original directional projection has the same fourth-moment ratio bound, because for arbitrary original coefficients \(b,c\),
\[
b(X-j)+c(Y-k)=-b(A-1)+k(c-hb)(Y/k-1).
\]

For every integer \(M\ge1\), take independent original rows \((X_i,Y_i)\), allowing arbitrary integers \(h_i\ge2\), \(k_i\ge1\), \(j_i\ge100h_i(k_i+1)\), and \(L_i=j_i+h_ik_i+1\). Their original product mean \(\boldsymbol\mu=((j_i,k_i))_{i=1}^{M}\) belongs to their original product support. Every closed halfspace \(H\subseteq\mathbb R^{2M}\) containing \(\boldsymbol\mu\) has original product probability at least \(1/(4K)=1/545688576\). More precisely, for arbitrary real original block coefficients \(b_i,c_i\), the full centered sum \(T=\sum_{i=1}^{M}[b_i(X_i-j_i)+c_i(Y_i-k_i)]\) satisfies \(\mathbb ET^4\le K(\mathbb ET^2)^2\). When its variance is positive, each of \(\mathbb P(T>0)\) and \(\mathbb P(T<0)\) is at least \(1/(4K)\). When its variance is zero, \(T=0\) almost surely. All constants are independent of the number of rows, their parameters, and their original directions.
